summary: Irish Gauge is a fast, cutthroat 18xx-lite game where players auction shares in five railway companies and then any shareholder can build track, upgrade towns, or call dividends for a company they hold. It plays in about an hour and rewards reading when to trigger a dividend payout versus quietly building position first.
praised: strong player interaction despite companies being jointly owned
criticised: can feel swingy or chaotic with inexperienced players
initial confusion over letting any shareholder act on a company

interaction.detail: Players bid against each other for the right to take the next action, and crucially any shareholder can build track, upgrade a town, or call dividends for a company — so the five railway companies are fully shared state that everyone manipulates, not just their nominal owner.

scoring.why: It's a Winsome cube-rail/18xx-style game where shares are cashed in and the player with the most money at the end wins.
scoring.how_you_win: Buy and build up railway companies, collect dividends as they pay out, and end the game holding more total cash (from dividends plus your remaining share value) than any other player.
